positioning.verdict: Three role families is one too many for five months of experience. The evidence is all LLM application work; the backend role scores well only because DocQuery is a FastAPI service.

evidence_debt.risk: Rests on one duty-style bullet. Expect to be asked what the templates did and how you tested them.
A certificate with no project behind it. An interviewer who asks which services you have used gets no answer.
One bullet that says "worked on". Be ready to say which part you built.

plan.action: Push DocQuery to a public GitHub repository, deploy it on a free tier, and put both links on the resume and LinkedIn.
plan.why_this_one: No project in the profile has a link, and all six scored jobs rely on DocQuery or the internship as evidence. This makes the existing claims checkable.
plan.proof_artifact: A public repository and a live URL
jobs_unlocked: Generative AI Developer (Entry Level) (Lumen Forge AI)

plan.action: Add a pytest suite to DocQuery and run it in the existing GitHub Actions pipeline.
plan.why_this_one: pytest is the one missing must-have at Tallyroot, and it is what holds that score at 60 when the dimensions add up to 73.
plan.proof_artifact: A passing CI badge in the DocQuery README

plan.action: Rewrite the two weak bullets with the numbers the resume analysis asked for.
plan.why_this_one: The prompt-template bullet is the only evidence for a must-have at Orbitline, and it currently states a duty.

plan.action: Add one tool-calling agent to DocQuery and deploy it on AWS Lambda with Amazon Bedrock. Write the README with an architecture diagram.
plan.why_this_one: Hands-on AWS is missing in 3 of 6 jobs and agents in 2 of 6. One project closes both. A deployed project beats a second certificate here: the postings ask for hands-on work, which the existing certificate does not show.
plan.proof_artifact: A deployed endpoint and a README that names the AWS services used
